Issues.Title: Performance: reuse dynamic utility lookups across canonicalizeCandidates collapse groups
Issues.Body:
### Summary

In Tailwind CSS **4.3.3**, `canonicalizeCandidates(..., { collapse: true, logicalToPhysical: true })` repeatedly builds the same dynamic-utility alternatives when called for many class groups in a lint run.

A small experimental cache scoped to the **design-system object + SignatureOptions object + candidate string** reduced a canonical-rule-only lint workload from **12.3s to 10.7s**, and **12.1s to 10.5s**, in sequential A/B/A/B runs. This is a modest application-specific improvement, not a claim of a general 2x speedup or an end-to-end build improvement.

### Source hotspot

Tagged source: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/blob/v4.3.3/packages/tailwindcss/src/canonicalize-candidates.ts#L339-L375

Inside `collapseCandidates` → `collapseGroup`, a fresh `dynamicUtilities = new DefaultMap(...)` is created for every group. Its factory:

1. Looks up the candidate's relevant properties.
2. Iterates the functional utility roots.
3. Compiles/looks up replacements with the same value/modifier and builds property/value → replacement sets.

The underlying utility-property lookups are cached, but rebuilding and iterating this alternatives map is repeated. The factory appears to depend on the design system, signature options, and candidate—not the other candidates in the current group.

### Measurement setup

- Tailwind CSS 4.3.3; eslint-plugin-better-tailwindcss 4.9.1; Oxlint 1.87.0.
- Linux containers under Dagger, Node 26.12.1-slim.
- 769 web files. Native syntax lint remained enabled; only the Tailwind canonical-class rule was enabled among the Tailwind rules. Type-aware lint was disabled for this experiment.
- Default canonical rule options: collapse=true, logicalToPhysical=true, rem unspecified.
- Fresh Node/linter processes, same application source and configuration, sequential baseline/candidate/baseline/candidate in one container invocation.
- Both variants used the same instrumentation, including cumulative high-resolution timers and thread CPU counters. Absolute timings include instrumentation overhead and are not a rigorous general-purpose benchmark.
- The application corpus is not a standalone public reproducer; the source hotspot and regression examples below are the actionable parts of this report.

| Measurement | Baseline 1 | Candidate 1 | Baseline 2 | Candidate 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Oxlint-reported whole lint wall time | 12.3s | 10.7s | 12.1s | 10.5s |
| Canonical worker total, wall | 9.449s | 7.939s | 9.252s | 7.825s |
| canonicalizeCandidates calls, wall | 9.011s | 7.511s | 8.842s | 7.429s |
| canonicalizeCandidates calls, thread user+system CPU | 6.628s | 6.052s | 6.605s | 5.900s |
| Dynamic-alternatives factory evaluations | 5,937 | 905 | 5,938 | 905 |
| Dynamic factory, wall | 3.759s | 2.236s | 3.545s | 2.285s |
| Dynamic factory, thread user+system CPU | 2.137s | 1.622s | 1.983s | 1.615s |

All four full-corpus runs produced zero warnings/errors. Worker group counts varied slightly (~1,423–1,443) because the caller has a shared LRU and parallel file scheduling changes eviction order.

Additional attribution from an instrumented baseline:

- CSS/design-system loading was ~79ms, once—not the multi-second bottleneck.
- The first lazy canonicalization call took ~3.0s. That initialization cost remains with the candidate.
- Per-candidate canonicalization/cache lookup total was ~4.17s wall; full group collapsing accounted for another ~4.48s.
- The caller made 2,468 operation-cache lookups, with ~1,024–1,039 hits and only 14–29 eviction misses in representative runs. This was not mainly a too-small caller cache.
- Prefix IPC was measured separately (~0.4s wall in that baseline). The candidate does not optimize prefix handling.

### Minimal optimization sketch

Add one storage slot to the canonicalization DesignSystem interface:

~~~ts
[DYNAMIC_UTILITIES_KEY]: WeakMap<
  SignatureOptions,
  DefaultMap<string, DefaultMap<string, DefaultMap<string, Set<string>>>>
>
~~~

Then reuse the existing factory instead of changing its algorithm:

~~~ts
const DYNAMIC_UTILITIES_KEY = Symbol()

// Inside collapseGroup, after obtaining signatureOptions and the existing lookups:
const cache = (designSystem.storage[DYNAMIC_UTILITIES_KEY] ??= new WeakMap())
let dynamicUtilities = cache.get(signatureOptions)
if (!dynamicUtilities) {
  dynamicUtilities = new DefaultMap(/* existing candidate factory, unchanged */)
  cache.set(signatureOptions, dynamicUtilities)
}

// Keep the existing property intersections, linked candidates, combinations,
// signature equivalence tests, and complete group collapse algorithm unchanged.
~~~

The benchmark candidate made the equivalent narrow change to the installed ESM distribution in a temporary container. No application patch or rule removal is proposed.

### Semantics and cache lifetime

This is **not** a per-class canonicalization shortcut. Two individually canonical classes can still collapse together (e.g. px-2 + py-2 → p-2), and every complete group still goes through the existing collapse algorithm.

- Cache separation follows the same SignatureOptions identity as the existing property/signature caches, preserving distinctions such as rem, property expansion, and logical-to-physical handling.
- Cache storage belongs to the actual design-system object. Replacing/reloading that object yields an empty cache, just like the existing internal canonicalization caches.
- This does not introduce a new process-global stylesheet cache, and does not claim to fix the caller's existing stylesheet dependency invalidation. Persistent-editor/CSS reload behavior should receive upstream tests before adopting it.
- The new map retains alternatives until the design system is discarded; memory impact has not been quantified.

### Diagnostic equivalence checked

I compared the actual linter's complete JSON diagnostics before/after the candidate for fixtures containing:

~~~tsx
<div className="w-[1rem]" />
<div className="px-2 py-2" />
<div className="sm:px-2 sm:py-2" />
<div className="px-2! py-2!" />
<div className="flex-grow" />
<div className="ps-2 pe-2" />
<div className={"px-2 py-2 " + suffix} />
~~~

Both variants emitted **the same 10 diagnostics**, including single-candidate w-[1rem] → w-4 and flex-grow → grow, two-input collapse, variant/important handling, and concatenated-literal handling. The entire test was repeated with a real `prefix(tw)` stylesheet and tw:-prefixed classes: again **10 identical diagnostics**. JSON equality included messages, severities, file names and source spans. Autofix output and the full Tailwind upstream test suite were not tested.

Would a design-system-scoped cache for this particular lookup be appropriate upstream? The observed gain is useful but limited (~1.6s/~13% in this lint workload); the remaining lazy initialization and other canonicalization costs are deliberately not presented as solved.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Performance: reuse dynamic utility lookups across canonicalizeCandidates collapse groups" (#20634)

Issues.Title: Fix unshipped relative imports in `@tailwindcss/node` type declarations
Issues.Body:
Fixes #20631

## Summary

`@tailwindcss/node`'s `dist/index.d.ts` / `dist/index.d.mts` start with seven imports of modules the package doesn't ship (`./ast`, `./candidate`, `./compile`, `./intellisense`, `./theme`, `./utilities`, `./variants`), so consumers with `skipLibCheck: false` get TS errors.

They come from `__unstable__loadDesignSystem`'s inferred return type. Inferring it makes the declaration bundler follow `tailwindcss`'s internal `DesignSystem` type (which isn't exported from `tailwindcss`) into its source files, and those files end up as relative imports in the bundle.

This annotates the return type as `ReturnType<typeof ___unstable__loadDesignSystem>`, i.e. the type of the function imported from `tailwindcss`. The declarations now only import from `'tailwindcss'`, which consumers can resolve. No runtime change and no tsup config change.

## Test plan

Added `integrations/node/types.test.ts`. It installs the packed `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/node` tarballs into a project with `skipLibCheck: false` and runs `tsc` on a file that calls `compile()` and `__unstable__loadDesignSystem()`.

```sh
pnpm build
pnpm vitest --root=./integrations node/types.test.ts
```

- With this change: passes.
- With `compile.ts` reverted: fails, because of the seven unresolved imports.

The test uses `"target": "ESNext"` because the declarations also reference `Disposable` / `Symbol.dispose` (from `Instrumentation`), which need the ESNext lib. That's unrelated to this issue.

I ran this locally by building and packing only `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/node`, since I don't have the Rust toolchain set up. `vitest run packages/@tailwindcss-node` also passes. I haven't run the full suite.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Fix unshipped relative imports in `@tailwindcss/node` type declarations" (#20632)

Issues.Title: @tailwindcss/node: dist/index.d.ts imports ./ast, ./candidate and five more modules the package does not ship
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v4.3.3, and `main` at 8cc0551 (`@tailwindcss/node@0.0.0-insiders.8cc0551`)

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

None: `@tailwindcss/node` imported directly, type-checked with TypeScript 7.0.2

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

v26.12.1

**What browser are you using?**

N/A

**What operating system are you using?**

Windows

**Reproduction URL**

https://github.com/YevheniiKotyrlo/tailwindcss-node-declarations

**Describe your issue**

`@tailwindcss/node`'s `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.mts` start with seven imports of modules the package does not ship:

```ts
import { AstNode as AstNode$1 } from './ast';
import { Candidate, Variant } from './candidate';
import { compileAstNodes } from './compile';
import { ClassEntry, VariantEntry, CanonicalizeOptions } from './intellisense';
import { Theme } from './theme';
import { Utilities } from './utilities';
import { Variants } from './variants';
```

`dist/` holds no `ast`, `candidate`, `compile`, `intellisense`, `theme`, `utilities` or `variants` declarations, so a project that type-checks its dependencies' declarations (`skipLibCheck: false`) cannot import `@tailwindcss/node` without these errors. They look like `tailwindcss`'s internal `src/` modules: `src/compile.ts` and `src/urls.ts` import types from `../../tailwindcss/src/ast`, outside the package, and the declaration bundle keeps those paths as relative imports.

Steps:

1. Clone the reproduction and run `npm install`. It installs `@tailwindcss/node` and `tailwindcss` at `0.0.0-insiders.8cc0551`, TypeScript 7.0.2 and `@types/node` 26.6.5.
2. Run `npm run check`, which type-checks `index.ts` (`import { compile } from '@tailwindcss/node'`, then a `compile()` and a `build()`) with `strict: true`, `skipLibCheck: false` and `module`/`moduleResolution` `nodenext`.
3. Run `npm start`, which runs the same `index.ts` with Node.

Expected: step 2 reports no errors.
Seen: step 2 reports seven TS2307 errors, below; step 3 prints `true`, so only the declarations are affected. 4.3.3's `dist/index.d.ts` starts with the same seven imports.

```text
node_modules/@tailwindcss/node/dist/index.d.ts(1,38): error TS2307: Cannot find module './ast' or its corresponding type declarations.
node_modules/@tailwindcss/node/dist/index.d.ts(2,36): error TS2307: Cannot find module './candidate' or its corresponding type declarations.
node_modules/@tailwindcss/node/dist/index.d.ts(3,33): error TS2307: Cannot find module './compile' or its corresponding type declarations.
node_modules/@tailwindcss/node/dist/index.d.ts(4,63): error TS2307: Cannot find module './intellisense' or its corresponding type declarations.
node_modules/@tailwindcss/node/dist/index.d.ts(5,23): error TS2307: Cannot find module './theme' or its corresponding type declarations.
node_modules/@tailwindcss/node/dist/index.d.ts(6,27): error TS2307: Cannot find module './utilities' or its corresponding type declarations.
node_modules/@tailwindcss/node/dist/index.d.ts(7,26): error TS2307: Cannot find module './variants' or its corresponding type declarations.
```
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "@tailwindcss/node: dist/index.d.ts imports ./ast, ./candidate and five more modules the package does not ship" (#20631)

Issues.Title: Treat a lone CR and form feed as line breaks in the CSS parser
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The CSS parser skips the CR of a CRLF pair, but a lone `\r` (old Mac line endings, or the extra CR in `\r\r\n` you get when a CRLF file is converted to CRLF a second time) and a form feed are treated as regular characters. They end up in the buffer, so a file like this:

```css
@tailwind utilities;<CR>
.card {<CR>
  color: red;<CR>
}<CR>
```

fails with ``CssSyntaxError: Invalid declaration: `` `` (the leftover `\r` before `}` is parsed as a declaration), and `.foo,<CR>.bar` keeps the CR inside the selector.

[css-syntax-3 preprocessing](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-syntax-3/#input-preprocessing) maps CR, FF and CRLF to a single LF, and Lightning CSS and PostCSS both parse these files. This maps a lone CR and FF to `\n` at the top of the parse loop, next to the existing CRLF handling. The input length doesn't change, so source locations are unaffected.

## Test plan

Added a `Line endings: CR / CR CRLF / FF` test to `css-parser.test.ts` that parses an `@import`, a two-line selector and a rule with those line endings. All three fail on `main` with `CssSyntaxError: Invalid declaration` and pass with this change. `vitest run --project tailwindcss` passes (5165 tests).

I used Claude Code to write this change.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Treat a lone CR and form feed as line breaks in the CSS parser" (#20630)

Issues.Title: Load Lightning CSS lazily so `optimize: false` works without a native binding
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`@tailwindcss/node` imports `lightningcss` at module scope, so importing the package eagerly loads the Lightning CSS native binding. On platforms that don't have a published binding — OpenHarmony, for example — that throws while the module is imported, before `optimize` is ever consulted. As a result `tailwindcss({ optimize: false })` cannot be used at all on those platforms, even though no optimization was requested.

This moves the `lightningcss` load into `optimize(…)` and resolves it with a lazily created `require`, the same approach already used in `packages/@tailwindcss-node/src/index.ts`. The public `optimize()` signature stays synchronous and `Features`/`transform` are used as before.

The `require` is created from `__filename` in the CJS build and from `import.meta.url` in the ESM build, so both published bundles resolve `lightningcss` from the package itself.

## Test plan

- `pnpm vitest run packages/@tailwindcss-node` — 11 tests pass, including the new `src/optimize.test.ts`. The test makes the `lightningcss` ESM import throw and makes the lazy `createRequire(…)('lightningcss')` throw, asserting that importing `@tailwindcss/node` still succeeds and that `optimize(…)` only throws when it is called without a binding. A third case checks that `optimize(…)` still produces optimized CSS when the binding is available.
- Removed `lightningcss` from the package's `node_modules` to simulate a missing binding: both built artifacts (`dist/index.mjs` and `dist/index.js`) import/require successfully, and only `optimize(…)` throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. With the binding present, `optimize(…)` works in both formats.
- `pnpm exec prettier --check` on the changed files.

Fixes #20628
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Load Lightning CSS lazily so `optimize: false` works without a native binding" (#20629)

Issues.Title: Eager lightningcss import makes `optimize: false` unusable on platforms without a lightningcss binding (OpenHarmony)
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`@tailwindcss/node/dist/index.mjs` imports lightningcss at module scope:

```js
import { Features as ne, transform as en } from "lightningcss";
```

On OpenHarmony there is no `lightningcss-openharmony-arm64` package, and the prebuilt aarch64 musl binding uses `R_AARCH64_TLSDESC` relocations that the OHOS loader cannot resolve, so the Node process dies while importing `@tailwindcss/vite` — **even when the plugin is configured with `{ optimize: false }`**. The `optimize` option is only consulted later in `configResolved`, after the module (and lightningcss) has already been loaded.

## Expected

`tailwindcss({ optimize: false })` should not require the lightningcss native binding.

## Suggested fix

Load lightningcss lazily, only when `optimize()` actually runs, for example:

```js
async function optimize(...) {
  const { Features, transform } = await import("lightningcss");
  // ...
}
```

(or a lazily created `require` via `createRequire`, resolved inside the optimize path).

## Workaround

We currently provide a local stub package named `lightningcss-openharmony-arm64` so the eager import resolves to a JS pass-through. That keeps the build working, but CSS optimization is disabled and every consumer needs the same stub.

Version: `tailwindcss` / `@tailwindcss/vite` 4.3.3, Node 26.10.0.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Eager lightningcss import makes `optimize: false` unusable on platforms without a lightningcss binding (OpenHarmony)" (#20628)

Issues.Title: Preserve inline theme aliases during canonicalization
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Canonicalization temporarily disables `@theme inline`, but the resulting ASTs share the normal compilation cache. This can prevent `text-(--text-primary)` from becoming `text-text-primary` for an inline alias and make later CSS generation use `var(--color-text-primary)` instead of `var(--text-primary)`.

Keep temporary compilation in a separate cache partition and check variable preservation independently in each mode. This preserves existing namespace safeguards while fixing runtime aliases and subsequent CSS output.

Related: https://github.com/schoero/eslint-plugin-better-tailwindcss/issues/307

## Test plan

The new regressions cover minimal and light/dark stylesheets, ordinary and inline themes, cold and precompiled candidates, important utilities, and variables split across the two compilation modes. Four regressions fail on the unmodified base; all 13 pass with the fix.

Executed with Vitest 4.1.10:

```sh
node "$VITEST_BIN" run --configLoader native --config "$CORE_TEST_CONFIG" --silent=false --maxWorkers=1 \
  packages/tailwindcss/src/canonicalize-candidates.test.ts \
  packages/tailwindcss/src/intellisense.test.ts
```

`VITEST_BIN` is the installed Vitest entry point. `CORE_TEST_CONFIG` imports the package's `vitest.config.mts` and only redirects `cacheDir` for isolation. Both complete suites pass: 1,930 tests.

Prettier 3.9.6 also passes for the three changed files:

```sh
node "$PRETTIER_BIN" --check \
  packages/tailwindcss/src/design-system.ts \
  packages/tailwindcss/src/canonicalize-candidates.ts \
  packages/tailwindcss/src/canonicalize-candidates.test.ts
```

`PRETTIER_BIN` is the installed Prettier entry point.

Rust, browser, build, and integration suites were not run.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Preserve inline theme aliases during canonicalization" (#20624)

Issues.Title: Fix `SOURCEMAP_BROKEN` warning for Tailwind CSS roots in `@tailwindcss/vite` builds
Issues.Body:
## Summary

When Tailwind CSS isn't building source maps, the `@tailwindcss/vite:generate:build` transform returns the generated CSS with `map: undefined`. Rolldown reads that as "this plugin changed the code and lost the mappings", so any build with `build.sourcemap: true` that pulls the CSS into a JS chunk (e.g. `?inline`, or a worker environment like in the issue) warns with `SOURCEMAP_BROKEN`.

This returns `{ mappings: '' }` in that case instead, which is what Vite's own CSS plugins do when CSS source maps are off. When source maps are enabled the real map is still returned.

Fixes #20622

## Test plan

Added an integration test that runs `vite build` on Vite 8 with `build.sourcemap: true` and an `?inline` import of a Tailwind root. It prints the `SOURCEMAP_BROKEN` warning on `main` and is clean with this change. The rest of the Vite integration tests still pass.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Fix `SOURCEMAP_BROKEN` warning for Tailwind CSS roots in `@tailwindcss/vite` builds" (#20623)

Issues.Title: @tailwindcss/vite: build transform returns map: undefined, causing SOURCEMAP_BROKEN under Vite 8/Rolldown
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

`tailwindcss` 4.3.3, `@tailwindcss/vite` 4.3.3

**What build tool are you using?**

Vite 8.3.5 (Rolldown)

**Describe your issue**

In a build where any environment has `build.sourcemap: true` (here a Cloudflare Worker environment from `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`), Rolldown warns `SOURCEMAP_BROKEN` for the stylesheet that `@tailwindcss/vite` transforms.

The `@tailwindcss/vite:generate:build` transform returns `generate()`'s result as is, and `generate()` returns `{ code, map }` with `map` set to `undefined` unless source maps are enabled (`packages/@tailwindcss-vite/src/index.ts`, `Root.generate`). A transform that returns code with no map tells the bundler the mappings are lost.

Vite's own `vite:css` transform handles the same case by returning `{ mappings: "" }` when CSS source maps are off, which says the transform maps nothing, and no warning appears.

Setting `css.devSourcemap: true` only moves the warning to `vite:css`, and in our build it roughly doubled the CSS build time.

**Reproduction**

1. Vite 8 with `tailwindcss()` and a CSS file containing `@import "tailwindcss"`.
2. Any environment built with `build.sourcemap: true`.
3. Run `vite build` and see `SOURCEMAP_BROKEN` for the CSS module.

**Suggested fix**

Return `map: { mappings: "" }` instead of `undefined` when source maps are disabled.

**Workaround**

Wrap the plugin's `transform` and, for CSS ids only, replace a missing map with `{ mappings: "" }`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "@tailwindcss/vite: build transform returns map: undefined, causing SOURCEMAP_BROKEN under Vite 8/Rolldown" (#20622)

Issues.Title: Pin Bun in the half-upgraded v3 project upgrade test
Issues.Body:
tThis PR pins Bun to `1.4.3` in the `upgrades half-upgraded v3 project to v4 (bun)` integration test, that test currently fails on every run that actually executes.

the test installs `"bun": "^1.0.0"`, so it picked up Bun 1.4.4 when it came out on Oct 22, bun 1.4.4 copies the `overrides` from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` into `package.json` during `bun install`, the test harness puts pnpm-style keys like `@tailwindcss/node>tailwindcss` there. The next `npx @tailwindcss/upgrade` then fails because npm can't parse those keys:

```

```

## Test plan

I reproduced the behavior change with a minimal project (one dependency plus a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with an `a>b` override):

The `Linux / upgrade` integration job should pass on this PR

This small change was made using claude code

Issues.Title: Don't add whitespace around math operators inside strings in arbitrary values
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`addWhitespaceAroundMathOperators` runs on the whole decoded value and had no idea about quotes. So a string like `'(min(1,2))'` looked like a real `min(…)` call and came out as `'(min(1, 2))'`, which changes the text shown by `content-['(min(1,2))']`.

Quoted strings are now copied as-is, the same way `segment()` and `isValidArbitrary()` already skip them.

Fixes #20614

## Test plan

Added cases to `decode-arbitrary-value.test.ts`. They fail on `main` and pass with this change. Ran `pnpm vitest run` in `packages/tailwindcss`, all tests pass.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Don't add whitespace around math operators inside strings in arbitrary values" (#20615)

Issues.Title: Math-operator whitespace formatting mutates the contents of quoted strings in arbitrary values (e.g. content-['(min(1,2))'] outputs "(min(1, 2))")
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?** v4 (latest v4.x; also reproduced the decode stage against current `main`, see trace below) **What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) you are using?** `@tailwindcss/cli` (build-tool independent — the mutation happens in the candidate decoding stage) **What version of Node.js are you using?** v22 **What browser are you using?** N/A — output CSS is wrong before it reaches a browser **What operating system are you using?** macOS **Reproduction URL** https://github.com/rahul05ranjan/tw-string-arithmetic-repro **Describe your issue** An arbitrary value that is a **quoted string** gets its characters mutated when the string happens to contain something that looks like a math function call. Whitespace is added around commas and operators *inside the string literal*, changing the value the browser sees. Minimal class: ```html
…
``` Expected: ```css .content-\[\'\(min\(1\,2\)\)\'\] { content: "(min(1,2))"; } ``` Actual: ```css .content-\[\'\(min\(1\,2\)\)\'\] { content: "(min(1, 2))"; } ``` The element renders `min(1, 2)` instead of `min(1,2)`. Same with operators, e.g. `content-['(calc(1px+2px))']` → `content: "(calc(1px + 2px))"`. A control class whose string has no math-function name (`content-['(1+2)']`) is left untouched. What's happening: the `(` inside the string is scanned by `addWhitespaceAroundMathOperators` (`packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/math-operators.ts`) as if it started a real math call — it looks backwards for the function name, finds `min`, marks the region "formattable", and then adds the spaces for CSS formatting until the matching `)`. The decode pipeline calls it on the fully serialized value from `decodeArbitraryValue` (`packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/decode-arbitrary-value.ts`), and the value parser folds a quoted string into a `word` node, so the formatter receives the raw characters including the string's contents. The two helpers in the same folder — `segment()` and `isValidArbitrary()` — both explicitly skip over quoted strings for exactly this reason; `addWhitespaceAroundMathOperators` has no quote handling, so any `(` + math function name that occurs as plain text inside a string is treated as a real call. Verified against the decode stage on current `main`: ```js import { decodeArbitraryValue } from './packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/decode-arbitrary-value.ts' decodeArbitraryValue("'(min(1,2))'") // "'(min(1, 2))'" decodeArbitraryValue("'(calc(1px+2px))'") // "'(calc(1px + 2px))'" decodeArbitraryValue("'(1+2)'") // "'(1+2)'" (no math fn name → untouched) ``` The repro repo above has the three classes; `npm install && npm run build` regenerates the output. Suggested fix: when walking the input in `addWhitespaceAroundMathOperators`, skip over single/double-quoted regions (same approach as the `SINGLE_QUOTE`/`DOUBLE_QUOTE` handling in `segment.ts`).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Math-operator whitespace formatting mutates the contents of quoted strings in arbitrary values (e.g. content-['(min(1,2))'] outputs "(min(1, 2))")" (#20614)

Issues.Title: Rewrite `url(…)`s next to an `image-set(…)` when inlining imported stylesheets
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`rewriteUrlsInAst` picks a single rewriter per declaration. When a value has both `url(…)` and `image-set(…)`, only the `image-set(…)` rewriter runs, and it copies everything around its match as-is. So the sibling `url(…)`s in an imported stylesheet are never rebased:

```css
/* src/components/hero.css, imported from src/app.css */
.hero { background-image: url(./overlay.png), image-set("./bg.png" 1x); }
/* before: url(./overlay.png), image-set(url("./components/bg.png") 1x) */
/* after:  url(./components/overlay.png), image-set(url("./components/bg.png") 1x) */
```

In Vite, `./overlay.png` is then resolved against `app.css`. Vite warns that it "didn't resolve at build time" and the image is not emitted. Vite fixed this in its own copy of this code in vitejs/vite#18868. Porting that fix as-is would rebase the URLs inside `image-set(…)` twice here, because our rebased paths stay relative. Instead, `asyncReplace` takes an optional replacer for the text between matches, and `rewriteCssImageSet` uses it for the `url(…)`s outside the `image-set(…)`. Each URL is now rewritten exactly once.

## Test plan

- New test in `urls.test.ts`. It fails on `main` (`url(./a.png)` and `url("./d.png")` are left as-is) and passes with this change. It also checks that `url(./b.png)` inside the `image-set(…)` is rebased only once.
- `vitest run --project @tailwindcss/node --project @tailwindcss/postcss`: 32 passed. Full `vitest run --hideSkippedTests`: 5657 passed, 1 skipped.
- Vite 8 build with `@tailwindcss/vite` and the stylesheet above: on `main` it warns and drops `overlay.png`. With this change both images are emitted and there are no warnings.
- `prettier --check` on the changed files.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Rewrite `url(…)`s next to an `image-set(…)` when inlining imported stylesheets" (#20612)

Issues.Title: Reject bare color opacity modifiers above 100
Issues.Body: ## Summary Bare opacity modifiers only check if the value isn't negative or it's a multiple of `0.25`, with none validation for values above `100`for opacity, so `bg-red-500/150` generates a bad value like `color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-red-500) 150%, transparent)`, browser rejects `color-mix()` percentages above 100%, so the declaration is silently dropped The solution is rejecting bare values above 100 in `asColor()` which also covers the `shadow`, `inset-shadow`, `text-shadow` and `drop-shadow`, the shared `isValidOpacityValue` is unchanged because `opacity-150` or `backdorp-opacity-150` are valid, browser clamps them [Tailwind play with some evidences](https://play.tailwindcss.com/7h69kLB7ZL) ## Test plan - New test invalid bare color opacity modifiers: checks that `/101`, `/150`, `/500`, `/100.25` and `/2.3` on color and shadow utilities generate no css, it fails when running against main - added `opacity-150` to the opacity test, checks that plain opacity still works above 100, `opacity: 1.5`, which the browser clamps `pnpm exec vitest run --project tailwindcss packages/tailwindcss/src/utilities.test.ts`

Issues.Title: Canonicalization: print utilities named `@` without a `-` after the `@`
Issues.Body:
## Summary

When a plugin registers a utility named `@`, `@px-4` can also be parsed as root `@` with value `px-4`. `printCandidate` always put a `-` between root and value, so that reading printed as `@-px-4`, and canonicalization returned it as the "canonical" form. That class doesn't compile (and `@--foo-4` became `@---foo-4`, which sets a different property).

This skips the `-` for a utility named `@`, the same way `printVariant` already does for the `@` variant. Now both readings print back as the original class and nothing gets rewritten.

Fixes #20607

## Test plan

Added a regression test in `canonicalize-candidates.test.ts` using the plugin from the issue. It fails on `main` (`['@-px-4', '@---foo-4']`) and passes with this change. Ran `pnpm vitest run` in `packages/tailwindcss`, all tests pass.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Canonicalization: print utilities named `@` without a `-` after the `@`" (#20608)

Issues.Title: canonicalizeCandidates rewrites every `@…` utility once a plugin registers a utility named `@`
Issues.Body:
## Versions

- tailwindcss 4.3.3 (also `@tailwindcss/node` 4.3.3, via `__unstable__loadDesignSystem`)
- Seen first through Tailwind CSS IntelliSense's "canonical class" suggestion, which uses the same API
- Node 24 and Bun 1.3 on macOS give the same result; nothing in the path is platform-specific

## What happens

A plugin registers two functional utilities: an ordinary one whose name starts with `@` (`@px`), and
one named exactly `@` that accepts only values starting with `--` (to support `@--foo-4`).
`canonicalizeCandidates()` then proposes, for every `@…` class, a spelling with a `-` inserted after
the `@`. The proposal either does not compile or compiles to something else:

| input      | compiles to          | proposed canonical | proposal compiles to   |
| ---------- | -------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------- |
| `@px-4`    | `padding-inline:4px` | `@-px-4`           | nothing                |
| `@--foo-4` | `--foo:4`            | `@---foo-4`        | `---foo:4` (other var) |

In our real plugin, where `@mt` also has a negative twin `@-mt`, `@mt-16/24` is proposed as
`@-mt-16/24` — the negated value.

## Minimal repro

```js
// plugin.mjs
import plugin from 'tailwindcss/plugin'

export default plugin(({ matchUtilities }) => {
  matchUtilities(
    { '@px': (value) => ({ 'padding-inline': `${value}px` }) },
    { values: { __BARE_VALUE__: (v) => v.value } },
  )
  matchUtilities(
    { '@': (value) => ({ [value.replace(/-\d+$/, '')]: value.match(/\d+$/)?.[0] ?? '0' }) },
    { values: { __BARE_VALUE__: (v) => (v.value.startsWith('--') ? v.value : undefined) } },
  )
})
```

```js
// run.mjs — with tailwindcss@4.3.3 and @tailwindcss/node@4.3.3 installed; `node run.mjs`
import { __unstable__loadDesignSystem } from '@tailwindcss/node'

const ds = await __unstable__loadDesignSystem(`@import 'tailwindcss'; @plugin './plugin.mjs';`, {
  base: import.meta.dirname,
})
for (const c of ['@px-4', '@--foo-4']) {
  const [canon] = ds.canonicalizeCandidates([c])
  const readings = ds.parseCandidate(c).map((p) => `${p.root} + ${p.value?.value}`)
  console.log(`${c} | readings: ${readings.join(', ')} | canonical: ${canon}`)
  console.log(`  ${JSON.stringify(ds.candidatesToCss([c])[0])}`)
  console.log(`  ${JSON.stringify(ds.candidatesToCss([canon])[0])}`)
}
```

Output, verbatim:

```
@px-4 | readings: @px + 4, @ + px-4 | canonical: @-px-4
  ".\\@px-4 {\n  padding-inline: 4px;\n}\n"
  null
@--foo-4 | readings: @ + --foo-4 | canonical: @---foo-4
  ".\\@--foo-4 {\n  --foo: 4;\n}\n"
  ".\\@---foo-4 {\n  ---foo: 4;\n}\n"
```

## Expected

`canonicalizeCandidates(['@px-4'])` returns `['@px-4']`, and `['@--foo-4']` returns `['@--foo-4']`:
a canonical form is only offered when it compiles to the same CSS as the input, and printing a
parsed candidate gives back the candidate it was parsed from.

## The code path (read in the built `dist/lib.mjs` of 4.3.3)

1. **Root search.** For utilities, the function that yields `[root, value]` splits (`findRoots`)
   ends with `e[0] === "@" && has("@") && (yield ["@", e.slice(1)])` — a candidate starting with `@`
   gets an extra reading with root `@` and no separator, whenever a utility named `@` exists.
   `@px-4` therefore parses twice: root `@px` value `4`, and root `@` value `px-4`.
2. **Printing.** `printCandidate` writes a functional utility as `root + "-" + value` unconditionally.
   `printVariant` has the matching special case (`let hasDash = root !== "@"`), but the utility
   printer does not, so the root-`@` reading prints as `@-px-4` / `@---foo-4` — not the string it was
   parsed from.
3. **Canonicalisation.** The last step of the candidate pipeline iterates over every reading from
   `parseCandidate()`, applies the transforms, prints, and returns the first print that differs from
   the input. The first reading prints back unchanged, so the second one's non-round-tripping print
   is returned. This step does not compare the signature of the result with the input's, unlike the
   steps that look up replacement utilities (which check signature equality before replacing).

Any one of these would stop it: skip the root-`@` reading in step 1 when the candidate does not
otherwise parse that way (as the variant path does), omit the `-` after a root of `@` in step 2 as
`printVariant` does, or require equal signatures before step 3 returns a different print.

## Workaround

Register the `@`-named utility as `@-` instead. Tailwind splits `@--foo-4` into root `@-` and value
`foo-4` (put the `--` back in `__BARE_VALUE__`); no other `@…` candidate can reach a root `@-`, so
the extra reading disappears and every class compiles to the same CSS as before.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "canonicalizeCandidates rewrites every `@…` utility once a plugin registers a utility named `@`" (#20607)

Issues.Title: Fix incremental WASI source scanning
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fix incremental source discovery in the WASI scanner.

This surfaced in a Vite dev server running inside WebContainer, which uses the WASI binding. Changing a utility class in JSX (for example, `bg-red-600` to `bg-blue-600`) updated the markup, but the new utility was missing from the generated CSS. The filesystem change event arrived and Vite reran the Tailwind CSS transform, yet the reused scanner no longer reported the source files or discovered the new class.

Touching the stylesheet, even by adding a comment, made the missing styles appear because it caused Tailwind to recreate the scanner. A fresh production build also generated the expected CSS. The issue was reproduced independently of Vite and WebContainer by reusing the WASI scanner in a standalone Node.js process.

The first scan uses synchronous directory traversal, but subsequent scans switch to the parallel walker. In the vendored `ignore` crate, the parallel walker's directory-entry constructors return `unsupported platform` on targets other than Unix and Windows. Those errors are skipped, so subsequent scans lose the discovered file list and fail to detect changed or newly added files while continuing to return cached candidates.

Keep synchronous traversal on those targets. Unix and Windows retain the existing initial-synchronous/subsequent-parallel strategy. This changes directory traversal only; the scanner's other parallel processing paths are unchanged.

Add a WASI regression covering an unchanged rescan, an edited source file, and a newly added nested source file. Explicit modification times avoid depending on filesystem timestamp resolution or sleeps.

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p tailwindcss-oxide` — 196 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @tailwindcss/oxide run build:wasm` — rebuilt the release WASI binding.
- Exercised the repeated-scan scenario directly against the rebuilt binding in Node WASI. Before the fix, the unchanged second scan lost `index.html` and later scans missed edits and additions. After the fix, all four scan states retained the expected files and candidates.
- `cargo fmt --package tailwindcss-oxide -- --check` — passed.
- `pnpm exec prettier --check integrations/oxide/wasm.test.ts` — passed.

The new integration test follows the existing Linux-only WASI test gating. Its scanner lifecycle was exercised directly on macOS; the packaged integration suite was not run locally.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Fix incremental WASI source scanning" (#20605)

Issues.Title: Don't treat the `/` in theme keys like `width.1/2` as an opacity modifier
Issues.Body:
## Summary

In v4, `theme()` always reads the part after the last `/` as an opacity modifier. For theme keys that contain a `/`, like the fraction keys in the default compat theme, `theme(width.1/2)` resolves `width.1` instead and applies `2` as the alpha:

```css
.half {
  width: theme(width.1/2);
}
```

compiles to `width: color-mix(in oklab, 0.25rem 200%, transparent)` on 4.3.3 and on `main`. The plugin API's `theme('width.1/2')` returns the same value, while `theme('width')['1/2']` returns the expected width. v3.4.19 compiles the CSS above to `width: 50%`, and the 4.0 changelog lists referencing `--width-1\/2` as `theme('width.1/2')` as supported (#14739), so this mostly affects CSS and plugins carried over from v3.

`createThemeFn` now resolves the full path first and only splits off the last segment as a modifier when the full path doesn't resolve. `theme(colors.red.500/50%)` and the existing `theme(colors.red.500 / 75%)` test behave as before.

## Test plan

- Added `theme(width.1/2)` to `css-functions.test.ts` (a `--width-1\/2` CSS variable, `inset.1/3` from the default compat theme, and a `colors.red.500/50%` control) and a plugin API test in `compat/plugin-api.test.ts` (CSS variable, JS config `extend`, default compat theme, and a color control). Both fail on `main` with the `color-mix(...)` values and pass with this change.
- `npx vitest run` in `packages/tailwindcss`: 44 files, 5164 passed, 1 skipped.
- `prettier --check` on the changed files passes.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Don't treat the `/` in theme keys like `width.1/2` as an opacity modifier" (#20604)

Issues.Title: Canonicalization: collapse `text-{x} leading-none` into `text-{x}/none` consistently
Issues.Body:
## Summary

With `collapse: true`, `text-xs leading-none` only became `text-xs/none` if `text-xs/none` had been seen earlier by the same design system, so the result depended on what was canonicalized before.

When candidates set a `line-height`, the collapse step pre-computes the matching `text-{x}/{y}` utilities, but only for spacing multipliers and arbitrary values. The `none` modifier isn't a `--leading-*` theme key, so `text-{x}/none` is never in the class list either, and it was only known once something else compiled it. Now a `line-height` of `1` also pre-computes `text-{x}/none` (and `text-[…]/none` for arbitrary font sizes), so `text-xs leading-none` always becomes `text-xs/none`.

Fixes #20602

## Test plan

- Added `text-xs leading-none` → `text-xs/none` and `text-[13px] leading-none` → `text-[13px]/none` to the shorthand tests in `canonicalize-candidates.test.ts`. They fail on `main` and pass with this change.
- Checked the issue's case on a fresh design system and after canonicalizing `text-xs/none flex` first, both now give `text-xs/none`.
- `pnpm vitest run` in `packages/tailwindcss` passes.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Canonicalization: collapse `text-{x} leading-none` into `text-{x}/none` consistently" (#20603)

Issues.Title: `canonicalize` collapse still depends on previously processed candidates (`text-xs leading-none` → `text-xs/none`)
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v4.3.3, and `0.0.0-insiders.8cc0551` (main as of 2026-10-19)

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

CLI only (`tailwindcss canonicalize --stream`). The same happens with `designSystem.canonicalizeCandidates(…, { collapse: true })` from `__unstable__loadDesignSystem`.

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

v26.12.0

**What browser are you using?**

N/A

**What operating system are you using?**

macOS (arm64)

**Reproduction URL**

No repository needed; the default theme (`@import "tailwindcss";`) is enough.

**Describe your issue**

Whether `text-xs leading-none` is collapsed into `text-xs/none` depends on whether `text-xs/none` was processed earlier with the same design system.

```bash
# Alone: not collapsed
$ echo "text-xs leading-none" | tailwindcss canonicalize --stream
text-xs leading-none

# After a line containing text-xs/none: collapsed
$ printf "text-xs/none flex\ntext-xs leading-none\n" | tailwindcss canonicalize --stream
flex text-xs/none
text-xs/none
```

On v4.3.3 the result even follows the earlier spelling:

```bash
$ printf "text-[0.75rem]/none flex\ntext-xs leading-none\n" | tailwindcss canonicalize --stream
flex text-[0.75rem]/none
text-[0.75rem]/none
```

On main this third case prints `text-xs leading-none`, but the second case still collapses.

The earlier line has to contain more than one candidate. With `text-xs/none` alone on the first line, the second line stays `text-xs leading-none`.

The API shows the same behavior:

```js
const ds = await __unstable__loadDesignSystem(css) // default theme
ds.canonicalizeCandidates(['text-xs', 'leading-none'], { collapse: true }) // ['text-xs', 'leading-none']

const ds2 = await __unstable__loadDesignSystem(css)
ds2.canonicalizeCandidates(['text-xs/none', 'flex'], { collapse: true })
ds2.canonicalizeCandidates(['text-xs', 'leading-none'], { collapse: true }) // ['text-xs/none']
```

**Expected behavior**

The output for a class list does not depend on what was processed before it. Either `text-xs leading-none` always collapses into `text-xs/none`, or it never does.

**Impact**

We run `canonicalizeCandidates(…, { collapse: true })` in a formatter. A pre-commit hook formats only the changed files and CI formats all files, so the same class list was collapsed in one and not in the other. We stopped using `collapse` and pair the utilities ourselves for now.

**Related**

#19835 reported the same kind of order dependence with `px-[1.2rem] py-[1.2rem]` in `--stream` mode. #19837 fixed it by allowing arbitrary values to collapse, but, as that PR says, the cause is that processing a candidate registers the shorthand as a side effect. `text-xs leading-none` looks like another case with the same cause.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "`canonicalize` collapse still depends on previously processed candidates (`text-xs leading-none` → `text-xs/none`)" (#20602)

Issues.Title: feat(oxide): add FreeBSD arm64 native binding
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Adds a native `aarch64-unknown-freebsd` build of `@tailwindcss/oxide`.

FreeBSD arm64 currently has no native Oxide package, so it falls back to the `wasm32-wasip1-threads` scanner. That fallback can intermittently spin in the scanner. This adds native FreeBSD arm64 support alongside the existing FreeBSD x86_64 binding.

## Changes

Issues.Title: Decode single-digit hexadecimal CSS escapes
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`unescape` treats every two-character match as a simple character escape, including a backslash followed by a single hexadecimal digit. For example, `\a` becomes the letter `a` instead of U+000A, and `\0` becomes `0` instead of U+FFFD.

Distinguish hexadecimal escapes from simple escapes using separate capture groups. This preserves the existing handling of one-to-six hex digits, optional trailing whitespace, and invalid code points.

This also fixes theme variable normalization: `@theme { --color-\0: red; }` currently registers `--color-0`, while the CSS reference `var(--color-\0)` refers to a different identifier. Add a compilation regression test alongside the helper tests.

Reference: [CSS Syntax — consume an escaped code point](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-syntax-3/#consume-escaped-code-point).

## Test plan

- With the original implementation, the nine new single-digit helper cases and the new compilation case fail.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project tailwindcss packages/tailwindcss/src/utils/escape.test.ts` — 19 passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project tailwindcss packages/tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts -t 'single-digit hexadecimal'` — 1 passed.
- Prettier check on all three changed files — passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project tailwindcss` — 5,158 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped. The same three snapshot failures were verified on unmodified upstream `f7f47f8`: CSS mixins, rounded utilities, and theme string indexing.
- Full Rust/build verification has not been run; the partial workspace typecheck limitation noted during setup remains.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Decode single-digit hexadecimal CSS escapes" (#20591)

Issues.Title: Canonicalization: only ignore `--tw-{property}` next to the related property
Issues.Body:
This PR fixes an issue where `canonicalizeCandidates` with `collapse: true` can drop a utility that sets a `--tw-*` variable, which loses CSS.

When we compute the signature of a utility, we ignore a `--tw-{property}` declaration if `{property}` exists with the same value (since https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/19156). This way `[font-weight:400]` can become `font-normal`, even though `font-normal` also sets `--tw-font-weight: 400`.

But the check did not compare the property names. It ignored a `--tw-*` declaration when _any_ other property had the same value. With this custom utility:

```css
@utility link {
  margin-top: 16px;
  --tw-translate-x: 16px;
}
```

The signature of `link` was the same as the one of `mt-4`, so `link mt-4` became `mt-4`. The output CSS then has no `--tw-translate-x: 16px`, and an element with `link mt-4 translate-y-2` moves 0 instead of 16px on the x axis.

The check now only matches the related property: `{property}` for `--tw-{property}`. A few core utilities set a variable with another name, so these map explicitly:

- `--tw-leading` → `line-height`
- `--tw-tracking` → `letter-spacing`
- `--tw-duration` → `transition-duration`
- `--tw-ease` → `transition-timing-function`

I found these with a scan of all utilities in `getClassList()` with the default theme, for each `--tw-*` declaration that has a sibling with the same value. All other matches in core use the same name (`--tw-font-weight`, `--tw-border-style`, `--tw-outline-style`, `--tw-content`). The scan also found `--tw-space-x-reverse: 0` next to `margin-inline-*: 0` for `space-x-0`, which is not related, and which is now part of the signature.

If a new core utility sets a `--tw-*` variable next to a property with another name and it is not in this list, it only canonicalizes less. It does not drop CSS.

## Test plan

- Added a regression test to `canonicalize-candidates.test.ts`. On `main`, `link mt-4` becomes `mt-4`. With this change, it stays `link mt-4`.
- The existing tests that need the check still pass, without a change to their expectations (e.g. `[font-weight:400]` → `font-normal`, `[line-height:0]` → `leading-0`, `text-sm leading-7` → `text-sm/7`).
- All tests in `packages/tailwindcss` pass, and `pnpm run build` passes.

<sub>Sent by an AI assistant on behalf of @RobinMalfait.</sub>
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Canonicalization: only ignore `--tw-{property}` next to the related property" (#20593)

Issues.Title: Add changelog fragments in `.changelog/`
Issues.Body:
This PR adds changelog fragments, so that pull requests do not conflict with each other in `CHANGELOG.md`.

Each pull request that needs a changelog entry adds a Markdown file to `.changelog/`, for example `.changelog/vite-full-reload.md`:

```md
### Fixed

- Prevent `@tailwindcss/vite` from doing a full page reload for external files (e.g. `.php` files)
```

The entry needs no link to the pull request. The script finds the pull request that added the fragment in the git history, and adds its link. An entry that already has a `[#…](…)` link keeps it.

## Changes

- `scripts/changelog.mjs` has three commands (also as `pnpm changelog`):
  - `pnpm --silent changelog` prints `CHANGELOG.md`, with the entries of the fragments in `[Unreleased]`.
  - `pnpm changelog check` validates the fragments and the `[Unreleased]` section.
  - `pnpm changelog release <version> [<date>]` moves the entries into a new `## [<version>] - <date>` section, updates the compare links, and deletes the fragments.
- The entries that are already in `[Unreleased]` come first. The entries of the fragments follow, in the order in which their pull requests merged. Thus the current entries in `CHANGELOG.md` keep working during the transition.
- A new `Changelog` job in `ci.yml` runs `check`. It only needs Node.js, and it is not a required check.
- A new `changelog.yml` workflow pushes the preview to the `changelog` branch after each merge into `main` that changes the fragments, `CHANGELOG.md` or the script. The branch has one commit with only `CHANGELOG.md`. `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` links to this preview.
- `.changelog/README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` explain the format.
- The tests are in `scripts/changelog.test.mjs`, in a new `scripts` vitest project.

## Test plan

- `pnpm vitest run --project scripts`
- `node ./scripts/changelog.mjs check`
- After the merge, run the `Changelog preview` workflow and check the `changelog` branch.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Add changelog fragments in `.changelog/`" (#20592)
